[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=61.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "dependency-migration-mcp"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "MCP server: through-the-upgrade dependency-migration briefs for LLM coding agents (the non-mechanical residue codemods don't cover + stale-API hallucination correction)."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
    "mcp>=1.2.0",
    "pydantic>=2.0",
]

[project.scripts]
dependency-migration-mcp = "dependency_migration_mcp.server:main"

[tool.setuptools]
packages = ["dependency_migration_mcp", "dependency_migration_mcp.data"]

"""dependency_migration_mcp — through-the-upgrade briefs for LLM coding agents."""

__version__ = "0.1.0"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""MCP server: through-the-upgrade dependency-migration briefs.

Positioning: official codemods auto-apply the mechanical ~90% of a major
version bump. This server briefs an LLM coding agent on the NON-mechanical
~10% that still leaves the build red, and corrects the agent's stale-training
hallucination of the old API surface — the part a codemod cannot do.

Exposes ONE tool: `get_migration(package, from_version, to_version)`.
"""

from typing import Any

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator

from .data import lookup, normalize_version, supported_matrix

mcp = FastMCP("dependency_migration_mcp")

POSITIONING = (
    "Official codemods handle the mechanical ~90%; this brief is the "
    "non-mechanical ~10% that still leaves the build red, plus the "
    "stale-training hallucination corrections a codemod cannot do."
)

VALID_CATEGORIES = {
    "mechanical",
    "non-mechanical",
    "behavioural",
    "removed-api",
    "config-shape",
}


class GetMigrationInput(BaseModel):
    """Input model for the get_migration tool."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        str_strip_whitespace=True,
        validate_assignment=True,
        extra="forbid",
    )

    package: str = Field(
        ...,
        description="Package name, e.g. 'tailwindcss', 'next', 'react' "
        "(aliases like 'tailwind', 'nextjs' are accepted).",
        min_length=1,
        max_length=100,
    )
    from_version: str = Field(
        ...,
        description="Version being upgraded FROM. Major number or any semver-ish "
        "string ('3', '3.4.1', 'v3', '^3') — only the major is used.",
        min_length=1,
        max_length=32,
    )
    to_version: str = Field(
        ...,
        description="Version being upgraded TO ('4', '15', '19', etc.).",
        min_length=1,
        max_length=32,
    )

    @field_validator("package", "from_version", "to_version")
    @classmethod
    def _not_blank(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if not v.strip():
            raise ValueError("must not be empty or whitespace only")
        return v.strip()


def _build_summary(dataset: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Top-level summary: counts, codemod, positioning, hallucination warnings."""
    changes = dataset["breaking_changes"]
    not_covered = [c for c in changes if not c.get("codemod_covered", False)]
    return {
        "total_changes": len(changes),
        "codemod_covered_count": len(changes) - len(not_covered),
        "not_codemod_covered_count": len(not_covered),
        "not_codemod_covered_ids": [c["id"] for c in not_covered],
        "codemod": dataset["codemod"],
        "stale_training_hallucination_warnings": dataset[
            "stale_training_hallucination_warnings"
        ],
        "positioning": POSITIONING,
        "source": dataset["source"],
        "verified_on": dataset["verified_on"],
    }


def _build_brief(dataset: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Assemble the full structured brief from a curated dataset entry."""
    changes = []
    for c in dataset["breaking_changes"]:
        assert c["category"] in VALID_CATEGORIES, c["category"]
        entry = {
            "id": c["id"],
            "title": c["title"],
            "category": c["category"],
            "what_changed": c["what_changed"],
            "find_occurrences": c["find"],
            "fix": c["fix"],
            "codemod_covered": c["codemod_covered"],
        }
        if c["codemod_covered"]:
            entry["codemod_command"] = c.get(
                "codemod_command", dataset["codemod"]["command"]
            )
        changes.append(entry)

    return {
        "status": "ok",
        "package": dataset["package"],
        "from_version": dataset["from_version"],
        "to_version": dataset["to_version"],
        "summary": _build_summary(dataset),
        "breaking_changes": changes,
    }


def _not_found(package: str, from_version: str, to_version: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Clean structured not_found — never raise for unknown pairs."""
    norm_from = normalize_version(from_version)
    norm_to = normalize_version(to_version)
    reason = "package/version pair is not in the curated dataset"
    if norm_from is None or norm_to is None:
        reason = (
            "could not parse a major version number from from_version/to_version"
        )
    return {
        "status": "not_found",
        "reason": reason,
        "requested": {
            "package": package,
            "from_version": from_version,
            "to_version": to_version,
        },
        "supported": supported_matrix(),
        "hint": (
            "Call get_migration with one of the supported (package, "
            "from_version -> to_version) pairs listed in 'supported'. v0.1 is a "
            "hand-curated dataset; long-tail coverage is roadmap."
        ),
    }


@mcp.tool(
    name="get_migration",
    annotations={
        "title": "Get dependency upgrade migration brief",
        "readOnlyHint": True,
        "destructiveHint": False,
        "idempotentHint": True,
        "openWorldHint": False,
    },
)
async def get_migration(params: GetMigrationInput) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a structured through-the-upgrade migration brief for a major bump.

    Use this mid-upgrade, right after bumping a dependency's major version and
    seeing the build go red (or before, to plan). It tells you which breaking
    changes a free official codemod will auto-fix vs. the non-mechanical residue
    you must handle by hand, how to find every occurrence in the user's own
    codebase, the concrete fix per occurrence, and which old APIs your training
    data will hallucinate.

    This does NOT run codemods or edit files — it is read-only briefing data.

    Args:
        params (GetMigrationInput): Validated input containing:
            - package (str): package name or alias (e.g. 'tailwindcss', 'next')
            - from_version (str): major version upgrading from (e.g. '3')
            - to_version (str): major version upgrading to (e.g. '4')

    Returns:
        dict: JSON-able structured brief.

        Success (status == "ok"):
        {
          "status": "ok",
          "package": str, "from_version": str, "to_version": str,
          "summary": {
            "total_changes": int,
            "codemod_covered_count": int,
            "not_codemod_covered_count": int,        # the part still red
            "not_codemod_covered_ids": [str],
            "codemod": { "command": str, "requires": str,
                         "covers": str, "does_not_cover": str },
            "stale_training_hallucination_warnings": [str],
            "positioning": str, "source": str, "verified_on": str
          },
          "breaking_changes": [
            {
              "id": str,
              "title": str,
              "category": "mechanical" | "non-mechanical" | "behavioural"
                          | "removed-api" | "config-shape",
              "what_changed": { "description": str,
                                "before": str, "after": str },
              "find_occurrences": { "guidance": str, "patterns": [str] },
              "fix": str,
              "codemod_covered": bool,
              "codemod_command": str        # present only if codemod_covered
            }
          ]
        }

        Not found (status == "not_found") — returned (never raised) for an
        unknown package or unsupported version pair:
        {
          "status": "not_found",
          "reason": str,
          "requested": { "package": str, "from_version": str,
                         "to_version": str },
          "supported": [ { "package": str, "from_version": str,
                           "to_version": str, "source": str,
                           "verified_on": str, "tier": str } ],
          "hint": str
        }

    Examples:
        - "I bumped tailwindcss to v4 and the build is red" ->
          get_migration(package="tailwindcss", from_version="3", to_version="4")
        - "Upgrading Next 14 to 15" ->
          get_migration(package="next", from_version="14", to_version="15")
        - Unknown pair (e.g. package="vue", "2"->"3") -> clean not_found with
          the supported matrix; no exception.

    Error Handling:
        - Empty/oversized inputs are rejected by the Pydantic model.
        - Unknown package or unsupported version pair -> structured not_found
          (status == "not_found"), NOT an exception.
    """
    dataset = lookup(params.package, params.from_version, params.to_version)
    if dataset is None:
        return _not_found(
            params.package, params.from_version, params.to_version
        )
    return _build_brief(dataset)


def main() -> None:
    """Entry point — stdio transport (local agent integration)."""
    mcp.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Curated, versioned migration dataset registry.

No runtime network calls — this is a hand-curated, spot-checked dataset. The
extraction/refresh cron pipeline is explicitly out of scope for v0.1.
"""

import re
from typing import Optional

from .nextjs import NEXT_14_TO_15
from .react import REACT_18_TO_19
from .tailwindcss import TAILWINDCSS_3_TO_4

# Registry keyed by (package, from_major, to_major). Versions are normalised to
# the major number because breaking-change deltas are defined per major bump.
_DATASETS = [TAILWINDCSS_3_TO_4, NEXT_14_TO_15, REACT_18_TO_19]

REGISTRY = {
    (d["package"], d["from_version"], d["to_version"]): d for d in _DATASETS
}

# Common alias spellings agents/users pass in.
_PACKAGE_ALIASES = {
    "tailwind": "tailwindcss",
    "tailwind-css": "tailwindcss",
    "tailwindcss": "tailwindcss",
    "next": "next",
    "nextjs": "next",
    "next.js": "next",
    "@next/next": "next",
    "react": "react",
    "reactjs": "react",
    "react.js": "react",
}


def normalize_package(package: str) -> str:
    """Lowercase, strip, and resolve known aliases to the canonical package name."""
    key = package.strip().lower()
    return _PACKAGE_ALIASES.get(key, key)


def normalize_version(version: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Extract the leading major version integer as a string.

    Accepts '3', '3.4', '3.4.1', 'v3', '^3.4', '~3', '3.x' -> '3'.
    Returns None if no leading integer can be found.
    """
    match = re.search(r"\d+", str(version).strip())
    return match.group(0) if match else None


def supported_matrix() -> list[dict]:
    """The list of (package, from -> to) pairs this dataset covers."""
    return [
        {
            "package": d["package"],
            "from_version": d["from_version"],
            "to_version": d["to_version"],
            "source": d["source"],
            "verified_on": d["verified_on"],
            "tier": "flagship (verified)"
            if d["package"] == "tailwindcss"
            else "reasonable-accuracy",
        }
        for d in _DATASETS
    ]


def lookup(package: str, from_version: str, to_version: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Return the raw dataset for a (package, from, to) triple, or None."""
    pkg = normalize_package(package)
    frm = normalize_version(from_version)
    to = normalize_version(to_version)
    if frm is None or to is None:
        return None
    return REGISTRY.get((pkg, frm, to))

"""Curated tailwindcss 3 -> 4 migration dataset.

VERIFIED against the upstream upgrade guide (https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide)
on 2026-05-16. This is the flagship, spot-checked package.
"""

TAILWINDCSS_3_TO_4 = {
    "package": "tailwindcss",
    "from_version": "3",
    "to_version": "4",
    "source": "https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide",
    "verified_on": "2026-05-16",
    "codemod": {
        "command": "npx @tailwindcss/upgrade",
        "requires": "Node.js 20+. Run on a clean branch; review the diff; test in a browser.",
        "covers": (
            "Dependency bumps, @tailwind -> @import, JS-config -> CSS @theme migration, "
            "utility renames (shadow/blur/rounded scale, opacity utilities), variable "
            "arbitrary-value syntax, prefix syntax, important-modifier position, package "
            "restructure (PostCSS/CLI/Vite). It also injects compatibility base styles for "
            "the changed border/ring/placeholder defaults."
        ),
        "does_not_cover": (
            "Semantic/behavioural changes that need a human visual decision (whether to KEEP "
            "v3 defaults via the injected compat shim or ADOPT the new v4 defaults), the "
            "space-y / divide selector change when you rely on inline elements or reversed "
            "order, hover-on-mobile, the browser-support floor, preprocessor removal "
            "(Sass/Less/Stylus), unsupported config options (corePlugins / safelist / "
            "separator), and @apply inside scoped Vue/Svelte/CSS-module styles."
        ),
    },
    "stale_training_hallucination_warnings": [
        "Your training almost certainly emits a `tailwind.config.js` / `tailwind.config.ts` "
        "with `module.exports = { theme: { extend: {...} } }`. In v4 there is NO config "
        "file by default — theme tokens live in CSS inside `@theme {}`. Only generate a JS "
        "config if the project explicitly keeps one via a `@config \"...\";` directive.",
        "Your training emits `@tailwind base; @tailwind components; @tailwind utilities;`. "
        "In v4 the entire entry CSS is a single line: `@import \"tailwindcss\";`.",
        "Your training emits opacity utilities like `bg-opacity-50`, `text-opacity-70`, "
        "`ring-opacity-*`, `border-opacity-*`. These DO NOT EXIST in v4 — use the slash "
        "modifier instead: `bg-black/50`, `text-black/70`.",
        "Your training emits the v3 size scale `shadow-sm` / `shadow` / `rounded` / `blur`. "
        "In v4 the scale shifted: `shadow-sm`->`shadow-xs`, bare `shadow`->`shadow-sm`, "
        "`rounded`->`rounded-sm`, `blur`->`blur-sm`. Emitting the old names produces a "
        "different visual result, not an error — so it slips past the build.",
        "Your training adds `autoprefixer` and `postcss-import` to postcss.config.js. v4 "
        "handles import-inlining and vendor-prefixing internally; the ONLY plugin is "
        "`@tailwindcss/postcss`.",
        "Your training emits CSS-variable arbitrary values as `bg-[--brand]`. v4 requires "
        "parentheses: `bg-(--brand)`.",
        "Your training runs `npx tailwindcss -i in.css -o out.css`. The standalone CLI moved "
        "to its own package in v4: `npx @tailwindcss/cli -i in.css -o out.css`.",
    ],
    "breaking_changes": [
        {
            "id": "tw-import-directive",
            "title": "@tailwind directives replaced by a single @import",
            "category": "mechanical",
            "what_changed": {
                "description": "The three @tailwind layer directives are replaced by one CSS @import.",
                "before": "@tailwind base;\n@tailwind components;\n@tailwind utilities;",
                "after": '@import "tailwindcss";',
            },
            "find": {
                "guidance": "Search every .css / .pcss / .scss entry file and framework <style> blocks.",
                "patterns": [
                    r"grep -rn '@tailwind' --include='*.css' --include='*.pcss' .",
                    r"grep -rn '@tailwind \(base\|components\|utilities\)' .",
                ],
            },
            "fix": 'Replace the three @tailwind lines with `@import "tailwindcss";`.',
            "codemod_covered": True,
            "codemod_command": "npx @tailwindcss/upgrade",
        },
        {
            "id": "tw-css-first-config",
            "title": "JavaScript config replaced by CSS-first @theme",
            "category": "config-shape",
            "what_changed": {
                "description": (
                    "tailwind.config.{js,ts} is no longer auto-loaded. Theme customisation "
                    "moves into the CSS `@theme {}` block using CSS variables. A JS config "
                    "can be retained only by explicitly loading it with `@config`. The "
                    "`corePlugins`, `safelist`, and `separator` options are NOT supported in v4."
                ),
                "before": (
                    "// tailwind.config.js\n"
                    "module.exports = {\n"
                    "  theme: { extend: { colors: { brand: '#1e40af' },\n"
                    "    fontFamily: { display: ['Satoshi','sans-serif'] } } },\n"
                    "  corePlugins: { preflight: false },\n"
                    "  safelist: ['bg-red-500'],\n"
                    "}"
                ),
                "after": (
                    '@import "tailwindcss";\n\n'
                    "@theme {\n"
                    "  --color-brand: #1e40af;\n"
                    '  --font-display: "Satoshi", "sans-serif";\n'
                    "}\n\n"
                    "/* OR keep the JS file explicitly: */\n"
                    '@config "../../tailwind.config.js";'
                ),
            },
            "find": {
                "guidance": (
                    "Locate tailwind.config.* and audit it for corePlugins / safelist / "
                    "separator — those have no v4 equivalent and need a hand-written "
                    "decision (drop them, or replicate via @utility / explicit classes)."
                ),
                "patterns": [
                    r"find . -name 'tailwind.config.*' -not -path './node_modules/*'",
                    r"grep -rn 'corePlugins\|safelist\|separator' tailwind.config.*",
                ],
            },
            "fix": (
                "Let the codemod migrate theme tokens into @theme (or emit @config to keep "
                "the JS file). Then MANUALLY resolve corePlugins/safelist/separator: "
                "corePlugins:{preflight:false} -> stop importing preflight via layered "
                "`@import \"tailwindcss/preflight\"` opt-out; safelist -> add the classes to "
                "a source file or use `@source inline(...)`; separator -> no replacement."
            ),
            "codemod_covered": True,
            "codemod_command": "npx @tailwindcss/upgrade",
        },
        {
            "id": "tw-opacity-utilities-removed",
            "title": "*-opacity-* utilities removed in favour of the slash modifier",
            "category": "removed-api",
            "what_changed": {
                "description": (
                    "bg-opacity-*, text-opacity-*, border-opacity-*, divide-opacity-*, "
                    "ring-opacity-*, placeholder-opacity-* are removed. Use the color "
                    "opacity modifier."
                ),
                "before": '<div class="bg-black bg-opacity-50 text-white text-opacity-70">',
                "after": '<div class="bg-black/50 text-white/70">',
            },
            "find": {
                "guidance": "Grep all template/markup files for the legacy opacity utilities.",
                "patterns": [
                    r"grep -rnE '\b(bg|text|border|divide|ring|placeholder)-opacity-[0-9]+' "
                    r"--include='*.html' --include='*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx,vue,svelte,astro}' .",
                ],
            },
            "fix": "Replace `<util>-opacity-<n>` by appending `/<n>` to the color utility.",
            "codemod_covered": True,
            "codemod_command": "npx @tailwindcss/upgrade",
        },
        {
            "id": "tw-utility-renames-scale",
            "title": "shadow / blur / rounded / drop-shadow scale shifted down",
            "category": "mechanical",
            "what_changed": {
                "description": (
                    "The default (unsuffixed) step now means the old `-sm`, and a new `-xs` "
                    "step is the old default. shadow-sm->shadow-xs, shadow->shadow-sm, "
                    "rounded-sm->rounded-xs, rounded->rounded-sm, blur-sm->blur-xs, "
                    "blur->blur-sm, drop-shadow-sm->drop-shadow-xs, backdrop-blur-sm->"
                    "backdrop-blur-xs. This is SILENT — wrong sizes render, the build stays green."
                ),
                "before": '<div class="rounded shadow-sm blur-sm">',
                "after": '<div class="rounded-sm shadow-xs blur-xs">',
            },
            "find": {
                "guidance": (
                    "Grep for the bare and -sm forms of shadow/rounded/blur/drop-shadow/"
                    "backdrop-blur. Be careful: a bare `shadow` must become `shadow-sm`."
                ),
                "patterns": [
                    r"grep -rnE '\b(shadow|rounded|blur|drop-shadow|backdrop-blur)(-sm)?\b' "
                    r"--include='*.{html,js,jsx,ts,tsx,vue,svelte,astro}' .",
                ],
            },
            "fix": (
                "Apply the scale map: *-sm -> *-xs, and bare * -> *-sm. Verify visually; the "
                "codemod handles class strings but not classes built by string concatenation."
            ),
            "codemod_covered": True,
            "codemod_command": "npx @tailwindcss/upgrade",
        },
        {
            "id": "tw-default-border-color",
            "title": "Default border color changed from gray-200 to currentColor",
            "category": "behavioural",
            "what_changed": {
                "description": (
                    "`border` with no color used to imply gray-200; in v4 an un-colored "
                    "border inherits currentColor. Borders that looked gray now take the "
                    "text color. The build stays green — this is purely visual."
                ),
                "before": '<div class="border px-2 py-3">  /* gray-200 border in v3 */',
                "after": (
                    '<div class="border border-gray-200 px-2 py-3">  /* be explicit */\n'
                    "/* OR globally restore v3 behaviour: */\n"
                    "@layer base { *, ::after, ::before, ::backdrop, "
                    "::file-selector-button { border-color: var(--color-gray-200, currentColor); } }"
                ),
            },
            "find": {
                "guidance": (
                    "Grep for `border` utilities WITHOUT an adjacent border-<color>. These "
                    "are the at-risk occurrences."
                ),
                "patterns": [
                    r"grep -rnE 'class=\"[^\"]*\bborder(-[0-9]+|-[xytrbl])?\b' "
                    r"--include='*.{html,jsx,tsx,vue,svelte,astro}' .",
                ],
            },
            "fix": (
                "DECISION REQUIRED (not mechanical): either (a) keep the codemod-injected "
                "compatibility base layer that pins border-color to gray-200, or (b) adopt "
                "the new currentColor default and add explicit `border-<color>` where the "
                "gray look mattered. The codemod injects (a) by default; choosing (b) is manual."
            ),
            "codemod_covered": False,
        },
        {
            "id": "tw-default-ring-width-color",
            "title": "ring default changed: 3px/blue-500 -> 1px/currentColor",
            "category": "behavioural",
            "what_changed": {
                "description": (
                    "The bare `ring` utility was 3px and blue-500 by default; in v4 it is "
                    "1px and currentColor. Focus rings shrink and change color silently."
                ),
                "before": '<button class="focus:ring focus:ring-offset-2">',
                "after": (
                    '<button class="focus:ring-3 focus:ring-blue-500 focus:ring-offset-2">\n'
                    "/* OR restore v3 defaults in CSS: */\n"
                    "@theme { --default-ring-width: 3px; --default-ring-color: var(--color-blue-500); }"
                ),
            },
            "find": {
                "guidance": "Grep for the bare `ring` utility (no width suffix, no color).",
                "patterns": [
                    r"grep -rnE '\bfocus:ring\b|\bring\b(?!-)' "
                    r"--include='*.{html,jsx,tsx,vue,svelte,astro}' .",
                ],
            },
            "fix": (
                "DECISION REQUIRED: replace bare `ring` with `ring-3 ring-blue-500` to keep "
                "the v3 look, OR set `--default-ring-width`/`--default-ring-color` in @theme, "
                "OR accept the thinner currentColor ring. Accessibility-sensitive — review focus states."
            ),
            "codemod_covered": False,
        },
        {
            "id": "tw-outline-none-hidden",
            "title": "outline-none now sets outline-style:none; old behaviour is outline-hidden",
            "category": "behavioural",
            "what_changed": {
                "description": (
                    "In v3 `outline-none` produced a transparent 2px outline (visible in "
                    "forced-colors mode for a11y). In v4 `outline-none` truly removes the "
                    "outline; the old accessible behaviour is now `outline-hidden`."
                ),
                "before": '<input class="focus:outline-none" />',
                "after": '<input class="focus:outline-hidden" />',
            },
            "find": {
                "guidance": "Grep for outline-none on focus/interactive states.",
                "patterns": [
                    r"grep -rn 'outline-none' --include='*.{html,jsx,tsx,vue,svelte,astro}' .",
                ],
            },
            "fix": (
                "If you used `outline-none` only to suppress the default ring before applying "
                "your own focus style, rename it to `outline-hidden` to preserve "
                "forced-colors accessibility. Use literal `outline-none` only when you truly "
                "want no outline. The codemod renames it, but confirm the intent per-site."
            ),
            "codemod_covered": True,
            "codemod_command": "npx @tailwindcss/upgrade",
        },
        {
            "id": "tw-space-between-selector",
            "title": "space-x/space-y (and divide) selector changed",
            "category": "behavioural",
            "what_changed": {

# dependency-migration-mcp

<!-- mcp-name: io.github.SolvoHQ/dependency-migration-mcp -->

**Through-the-upgrade migration briefs for LLM coding agents.**

Official codemods auto-apply the mechanical ~90% of a major version bump.
This MCP server briefs your agent on the **non-mechanical ~10% that still
leaves the build red**, and corrects the agent's **stale-v3-training
hallucination** of the old API surface — the part a codemod cannot do.

For one `(package, from, to)` triple it returns a structured brief: per
breaking change — category, before/after, how to grep every occurrence in
*your* code, the fix, and whether the free codemod already covers it — plus a
top-level list of the specific old-API hallucinations the agent must suppress.

## Supported matrix

| package       | from → to | tier | source |
|---------------|-----------|------|--------|
| `tailwindcss` | 3 → 4     | **flagship — verified** against the upstream upgrade guide (2026-05-16) | https://tailwindcss.com/docs/upgrade-guide |
| `next`        | 14 → 15   | reasonable-accuracy | https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15 |
| `react`       | 18 → 19   | reasonable-accuracy | https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide |

Versions are normalised by major (`3`, `3.4.1`, `v3`, `^3` → `3`). An unknown
package or unsupported pair returns a clean structured `not_found` (with the
supported matrix) — never an exception. Data is hand-curated and offline (no
runtime network calls).

## Install (one command, zero account)

```bash
uvx --from git+https://github.com/SolvoHQ/dependency-migration-mcp dependency-migration-mcp
```

That fetches, builds, and runs the stdio MCP server straight from public
GitHub. No clone, no signup, no API key. (Need `uvx`? `pip install uv`.)

Prefer pip? A venv fallback:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
pip install "git+https://github.com/SolvoHQ/dependency-migration-mcp.git"
dependency-migration-mcp        # runs the stdio server
```

## Tool

`get_migration(package: str, from_version: str, to_version: str) -> dict`

Read-only. Returns a JSON-able brief: `summary` (counts, codemod command +
what it does/doesn't cover, `stale_training_hallucination_warnings`,
positioning) and `breaking_changes[]` (each with `id`, `title`, `category`
∈ `{mechanical, non-mechanical, behavioural, removed-api, config-shape}`,
`what_changed.{description,before,after}`,
`find_occurrences.{guidance,patterns}`, `fix`, `codemod_covered`, and
`codemod_command` when covered).

Use it mid-upgrade: right after bumping a major version and seeing the build
go red, ask the agent to call `get_migration` before it starts editing.

## Smoke test

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt          # mcp>=1.2, pydantic>=2  (Python 3.10+)
python smoke_test.py
```

Imports the server, calls `get_migration("tailwindcss","3","4")` and asserts
the `@tailwind`→`@import` change, the CSS-first config-shape change, and a
stale-training hallucination warning are present; then asserts an unknown
pair returns a clean `not_found`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Smoke test for dependency_migration_mcp.

(a) imports the server (proves it constructs without error),
(b) calls get_migration("tailwindcss","3","4") and asserts the brief contains
    the @tailwind->@import change, the config-shape non-mechanical change, and
    at least one stale-training hallucination warning,
(c) calls an unknown pair and asserts a clean not_found (no exception).

Run: python smoke_test.py   (from the code/ directory)
"""

import asyncio
import json
import sys

from dependency_migration_mcp.server import (
    GetMigrationInput,
    get_migration,
    mcp,
)


def _check(cond: bool, label: str) -> None:
    status = "PASS" if cond else "FAIL"
    print(f"  [{status}] {label}")
    if not cond:
        raise AssertionError(label)


async def main() -> None:
    print(f"[a] Server imported OK. FastMCP name = {mcp.name!r}")
    _check(mcp.name == "dependency_migration_mcp", "server name correct")

    print("\n[b] get_migration('tailwindcss', '3', '4')")
    brief = await get_migration(
        GetMigrationInput(package="tailwindcss", from_version="3", to_version="4")
    )
    _check(brief["status"] == "ok", "status == ok")
    _check(brief["package"] == "tailwindcss", "package == tailwindcss")

    changes = brief["breaking_changes"]
    blob = json.dumps(brief)

    has_import_change = any(
        '@import "tailwindcss"' in c["what_changed"]["after"]
        and "@tailwind" in c["what_changed"]["before"]
        for c in changes
    )
    _check(has_import_change, "@tailwind -> @import change present")

    config_nonmech = next(
        (
            c
            for c in changes
            if c["category"] == "config-shape" and "config" in c["id"]
        ),
        None,
    )
    _check(
        config_nonmech is not None,
        "config-shape change present (CSS-first @theme)",
    )
    _check(
        "@theme" in config_nonmech["what_changed"]["after"],
        "config change documents @theme shape",
    )

    warnings = brief["summary"]["stale_training_hallucination_warnings"]
    _check(len(warnings) >= 1, "at least one hallucination warning")
    _check(
        any("tailwind.config" in w for w in warnings),
        "hallucination warning calls out tailwind.config (v3 shape)",
    )

    s = brief["summary"]
    _check(
        s["not_codemod_covered_count"] >= 1,
        "at least one NON-codemod-covered (non-mechanical) change",
    )
    _check(
        s["total_changes"]
        == s["codemod_covered_count"] + s["not_codemod_covered_count"],
        "summary counts are internally consistent",
    )
    _check(
        "non-mechanical ~10%" in s["positioning"],
        "positioning one-liner present",
    )
    print(
        f"      total={s['total_changes']} "
        f"codemod_covered={s['codemod_covered_count']} "
        f"NOT_covered={s['not_codemod_covered_count']} "
        f"warnings={len(warnings)}"
    )

    print("\n[b2] get_migration('next', '14', '15') sanity")
    nb = await get_migration(
        GetMigrationInput(package="next", from_version="14.2.3", to_version="v15")
    )
    _check(nb["status"] == "ok", "next 14->15 ok (semver-ish input normalised)")
    _check(
        any(c["id"] == "next-async-request-apis" for c in nb["breaking_changes"]),
        "next async request APIs change present",
    )

    print("\n[c] get_migration('vue', '2', '3') — expect clean not_found")
    nf = await get_migration(
        GetMigrationInput(package="vue", from_version="2", to_version="3")
    )
    _check(nf["status"] == "not_found", "status == not_found (no exception)")
    _check("supported" in nf and len(nf["supported"]) == 3, "supported matrix returned")
    _check(
        {p["package"] for p in nf["supported"]}
        == {"tailwindcss", "next", "react"},
        "supported matrix lists the 3 curated packages",
    )

    print("\nALL SMOKE CHECKS PASSED")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(main())
    except AssertionError as e:
        print(f"\nSMOKE TEST FAILED: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
